issueTitle: core,desktop:feat: dual planner + merger — two plans from shared findings synthesized into one with convergence report

plan.summary: Add a dual-planner + merger stage to the planning pipeline: two independent `generatePlan` runs over identical input (issue + optional aggregated findings) executed in parallel, then a tool-less structured merger call that emits the single canonical plan, a convergence score and a divergence list, plus a deterministic Jaccard sanity check computed in code. The desktop planner driver branches on a new global `multiAgentPlanning` setting (default off, today's flow bit-identical); the merged plan flows into the existing plan-store/confidence/gate path unchanged, with the merge report persisted alongside it for the next sub-issue (#264).

ambiguities.detail: Failure/degradation semantics when one planner run fails, both fail, or the merger call throws — the issue says nothing; the plan invents rules (one fulfilled → use it, merger throw → plan A, zero → rethrow).
Scale and meaning of the `convergence` score (0–1 vs 0–100, and what it measures) is unspecified.
Shape of `divergences[]` entries (free text vs structured fields like topic/planA/planB/severity).
Where the merge report (convergence, divergences, Jaccard) is persisted — alongside the StoredPlan envelope, separate store, or discarded — the issue only says 'stored alongside'.
How 'touched-file sets' are extracted from a plan for the Jaccard computation (which plan field, path normalization, empty-set edge case → Jaccard of two empty sets).
Default value and naming of the `Multi-agent planning` toggle setting (plan chose `multiAgentPlanning`, default off) and whether it is global or per-run.
Whether findings are required or optional input when the explorer fan-out produced none (plan made findings optional).
Which model/runtime the merger uses — the issue specifies the strong-model slot only for the planner role, not the merger.
Whether the two planner runs should be truly identical prompts (temperature/seed/sampling variation) so their outputs can meaningfully diverge.
Cost/latency handling: whether the two runs share a concurrency budget or token cap with the explorer fan-out.

clarity.rationale: The issue names concrete, checkable artifacts (two parallel planner runs, tool-less structured merger with plan/convergence/divergences, code-computed Jaccard, toggle, both-branch driver tests), but leaves scoring semantics, divergence shape, persistence location and all failure behaviour to the implementer — which the plan silently decided without flagging anything.

objections.detail: Step 5 says "if the merger throws, degrade to planner A's plan with `report` undefined rather than failing the whole run" — an unconditional catch. The merger is handed `opts.signal`, so an abort during the merge surfaces as a thrown AgentAbortError and would be swallowed, and the run would keep going (tripwire, scoring) on a cancelled lifecycle. This directly contradicts the plan's own risk #6 ("Aborts during ... the merger must propagate as AgentAbortError") and the #159 rule the driver's outer `catch (err) { if (err instanceof AgentAbortError || controller.signal.aborted) return; }` at apps/desktop/src/planner.ts:462-465 depends on. The `if (!live()) return` at planner.ts:421 bounds the damage to wasted work rather than a zombie write, which is why this is not blocking — but the merger catch must rethrow AgentAbortError (and re-check `opts.signal.aborted`), and planner-dual.test.ts should assert it.

Step 6 proposes emitting a second `{ kind: "status", phase: "agent-start", detail: "multi-agent planning — 2 planners" }` before the dual call. The driver already emits `agent-start` at apps/desktop/src/planner.ts:349, and `agent-start` is the planning stream's `resetPhase` — apps/desktop/src/event-stream.test.ts:84-97 asserts it wipes the replay buffer, and apps/desktop/src/plan-chat.test.ts:209 explicitly guards against a stray one. A second emit would discard the `worktree` and `graphify` status events already buffered for that run, i.e. the toggle-on path loses console history the toggle-off path keeps. Use a different phase/detail or move the existing emit, don't add a second `agent-start`.

The context claim "settings are stubbed via `getSettings: () => ({ ...DEFAULT_ORCHESTRATOR_SETTINGS, ...settings })` — that is the seam for testing both toggle branches" is wrong. In apps/desktop/src/planner.test.ts:378 the harness is `getSettings: () => ({ ...DEFAULT_ORCHESTRATOR_SETTINGS })` with no overrides parameter at all (makeRunHarness's options are item/prepareWorktree/providerName/extraItems, line 311-318), and its `askStructured` unconditionally throws (line 342-344) so critic/clarity degrade. Step 8's toggle-on test therefore needs real harness surgery: a `settings?: Partial<OrchestratorSettings>` option, an `askStructured` fake that distinguishes the merger call from computeConfidence's clarity/critic calls (they share the same provider), and `providerName: "claude-cli"` if the "only planner A carries sessionId" assertion is to be non-vacuous — the default `"fake"` name means no session is minted at all (planner.ts:316-318).

The merger's structured call carries no system prompt — `structuredCall` (packages/core/src/runtime/structured.ts:17-22) passes only prompt + schema + `tools: ""`, so PLANNER_SYSTEM_PROMPT never reaches it. That prompt is where the rules the groundedness signal actually grades live: files the plan creates must carry `status: "new"`, symbols a step creates go in `createdSymbols` and never in `symbols` (packages/core/src/planner/prompt.ts:94), plus the repo-conventions doc (#227) both planners get. Step 4's merge prompt only mentions "the same no-invented-paths/symbols rule". A merger that re-emits a created file without `status: "new"` or moves a created symbol into `symbols` produces a schema-valid plan that fails groundedness — and per packages/core/src/confidence/score.ts:152-153 a groundedness veto is decisive, so the toggle-on path can park items in needs-input that the single-planner path would have passed. The merge prompt must carry those structural rules verbatim (and `repoInstructions`).

The merger has no repair round. `generatePlan` goes through `validatePlanReply` (packages/core/src/planner/generate.ts:117-140), which exists precisely because a single structured reply of a full plan slips format often enough to warrant a cheap second round. The merger asks for strictly more in one tool-less turn (a whole plan plus convergence plus divergences) and, per step 5, a single `MergeError` silently discards planner B and the merge entirely — two agent runs paid for, plan A delivered. Reuse the repair round (or one retry) instead of a bare `safeParse` → throw.

Step 5 gives planner B no `sessionId` at all, citing the confidence extra runs. But the invariant those runs respect is that a claude-cli session id has one owner — not that a second run must be sessionless. The cost is concrete: `isSalvageableDeath` salvage (#194) is gated on `opts.sessionId` (generate.ts:172), so planner B cannot wrap up when it hits `plannerTimeBudgetMin` (default 15 min, planner.ts:385). Two planners racing in the same worktree makes a budget death *more* likely, and B is the run that cannot survive it — so the common failure is "paid for two runs, degraded to A". Minting B its own UUID (never persisted via setPlanSessionId, never streamed via onEvent) keeps single-ownership and keeps salvage. If sessionless is deliberate, say why in the plan; today it reads as an over-application of the confidence precedent.

Step 5 enumerates the options forwarded to both planners — "issue, repoPath, runtime, llm, findings, repoInstructions, graphify, confinement, hardTimeoutMs, preexistingChanges" — and omits `memory` and `maxTurns`. The current driver call passes `...(memory ? { memory } : {})` (planner.ts:396), i.e. the skipper-memory MCP the planner system prompt tells the agent to call before planning. If dual.ts builds its option objects from that enumeration rather than spreading `opts`, the toggle-on path silently loses memory retrieval for *both* planners — a behaviour regression versus the off path. Specify a spread of the shared options with only `sessionId`/`onEvent` differing.

`DualPlanResult.plans` is dead weight: the driver never reads it (step 6 destructures only `{ plan, report }`), and immediately after, `computeConfidence` spawns `settings.confidence.extraPlanRuns` *more* full planner runs to compute `scoreConvergence` (packages/core/src/confidence/score.ts:173-199). Toggle-on therefore costs 2 planners + merger + N extra planner runs on the same issue, and the convergence signal is computed against the *merged* plan (a synthesis of A and B) rather than the two real samples already in hand. Feeding planA/planB into `computeConfidence` as convergence samples is not the "convergence feeds the band" work deferred to #264 — it is avoiding paying twice for the same signal. At minimum the plan should say why it keeps `plans` in the return type if nothing consumes it.

`updatePlanBody` in apps/desktop/src/plan-store.ts:70-81 writes `{ ...stored, plan: <new>, editedAt, revisions: [...] }` — it spreads the whole envelope. So a `merge` report survives a chat-apply or inline edit (#165) and will describe a plan body that no longer exists, while `revisions[]` snapshots carry `confidence` but not `merge`. Since #264 is meant to consume `merge`, shipping it with no clear/snapshot rule bakes in a stale-report bug. Either drop `merge` on edit (like the semantics `confidence` gets via the revision snapshot) or document that it is generation-scoped and must be checked against `editedAt`.

The issue's own out-of-scope list names only "Convergence feeding the confidence band" and "UI for divergences" — it does not exclude the `Multi-agent planning` control itself, yet the plan defers it ("UI belongs to #264"), leaving the feature reachable only by hand-editing `<userData>/settings.json` or a raw IPC write. There is precedent for hand-editable-only settings (`confidence.extraPlanRuns` is documented "Hand-editable by design (#62)" at packages/shared/src/orchestrator.ts:170-171 and has no web UI), so this is defensible — but it is a scope narrowing the issue text does not grant, and it should be an explicit, stated assumption rather than an assertion that the UI belongs to another issue.
